'Apply for a fee waiver (conditional, required before filing): Unresolved.' leads a required-before-filing action with a one-word instruction that tells the participant nothing to do. The sentence immediately after it does explain ('Indigency waiver availability has not been confirmed') and page 4 names the clerk as the place to ask, so the block as a whole is honest and not misleading - which is why this does not fail FEE_AND_WAIVER. But the bare token as the lead of an action item is a participant-facing wording defect and should be replaced with the second-person form the rest of the block already uses. FIX04 disclosed it, which is what makes it reviewable.

recordsThatDisagree.item: 'The record held here does not state...'
recordsThatDisagree.vf36Position: AGREE, with a wording nit. 'The record held here' is factory phrasing, but both sentences are candid disclosures of a real gap and each is followed by actionable second-person direction ('Ask the clerk of the court you are filing in for the current civil filing fee'). Candour about what the packet does not know is worth more than the phrasing costs. Reword to 'This packet does not have...' when the block is next touched; do not remove.

The block is jargon to a participant, but it is a factory-wide legal disclaimer and rewording it in three of several hundred families would fragment it while fixing nothing. It belongs in a factory-wide change, not in a three-family repair. Flagging it here so the captain can see it is a corpus-level item rather than an Indiana one.

recordsThatDisagree.item: one petition per lifetime - roadmap sentence removed, judgement kept
recordsThatDisagree.fix04Position: kept 'when you file matters as much as what you file, get legal help with the timing' on the ground that it is true of the participant's decision and stop conditions 4 and 5 support it
recordsThatDisagree.vf36Position: AGREE, and this is the best call in the set. The withheld half ('Build the eligibility calendar and the 365-day window optimiser before the petition generator') is pure roadmap. The kept half is a true and load-bearing warning: one petition per lifetime under Sec. 35-38-9-9(i) plus a 365-day multi-county window means timing is genuinely decisive, and stop conditions 4 and 5 do carry it. Deleting it to be safe would have cost the participant the single most consequential piece of timing advice in the document.

recordsThatDisagree.item: Chastain - gate instruction removed, consequence kept
recordsThatDisagree.fix04Position: kept because it warns of irreversible harm
recordsThatDisagree.vf36Position: AGREE, firmly. 'Filing now can permanently cost you a record that becomes eligible later' is exactly what a participant must know before filing, and the harm is unrecoverable. The delivered sentence states the consequence and directs the reader to legal advice without asserting any court act. Keeping it was correct; removing it would have been the more dangerous error.
